author: blu
body: Infix arithmetic in a type. A proposition is parsed by parse-type, so without these two levels `1 + 1 === 2` stops at the operator: the type grammar returns the bare `1`, the claim parser then reads the `+` as the proof name, and the failure surfaces as CDX1000 on the token after it. The operator becomes an ordinary application spine -- `+` applied to two operands -- which is the shape ctype-to-aterm already carries into the proof normalizer, so nothing downstream needs a new node.

author: blu
body: Two levels rather than one because a single left-associative loop reads `1 + 2 * 3` as `(1 + 2) * 3`. The mul tail binds first and refuses to look at `+`; the add tail runs an operand through the mul tail before joining it, which is what keeps the grouping honest.

author: blu
body: Append is one level looser than the arithmetic, matching `&`'s precedence in expressions, and it exists for the same reason the two levels above it do: a proposition is parsed by parse-type, so without it `xs & Cons 7 Nil === ...` stops at the operator and the claim parser reads `&` as the proof name. Ampersand previously terminated every type parse, so the only sources this reaches are the ones that could not be written before.

author: blu
body: A wrapping band promises modular arithmetic the machine performs for free, and the machine performs it at the width of the store. When the band is the width the two agree; when it is narrower they do not, and the store truncates at the width and leaves a value outside the band in a field whose declared range the bounds prover goes on to trust. That makes an elided check rest on a false range, so the band is refused here rather than silently meaning something else. The token blamed is the mode keyword, because that is the word to delete.

author: blu
body: A negative literal is ONE atom, not a minus applied to something. The catch-all above takes the bare `-` and leaves the digits behind, which is why `-2` could never sit on either side of a `===`: the proposition `1 - 3 === -2` parsed its left side as subtraction and its right side as the name `-`, and no reduction could ever make those meet.

author: blu
body: This only fires where an atom is expected, so it cannot capture the `3` of `1 - 3`: by then parse-type-add-tail has already consumed the operator and the atom sees the digits alone.

author: blu
body: A quotation binds a local name to a definition named only by the digest of its content. The word joining the two is an ordinary word, not a keyword: the language is full of lists named as, including in this compiler, in the foreword, and in the reverse-reverse proof. It needs no protection, because the declaration it sits in has already been opened unambiguously.

author: blu
body: A trust floor sets the threshold for the whole chapter. It is carried through the header as a declaration like any other and sorted out at the end, because it may be written after the quotations it governs.

author: blu
body: A chapter declaring more than one floor gets the last one it wrote. A chapter declaring none is stamped with the negative sentinel the caller seeds, so the quotation gate can tell an absent floor from a declared floor of zero and refuse the former.

author: blu
body: But nothing checked the markers, and they drifted. The X86-64 chapter grew from ten files to thirteen; the three new ones never got a marker and M stayed at 10. Six of the seven multi-file chapters in the tree were coherent; that one was not, and no gate could tell.

author: blu
body: The cost of not checking is not untidiness. While a bare repeat is legal, an ACCIDENTAL duplicate chapter name is indistinguishable from a deliberate page: two chapters called Hamt in one quire merge under one slug, a name defined in both collides or shadows, and the program compiles and runs meaning something neither file said. Coherent pagination is what tells the two apart -- a real page declares itself one of M, and an accident does not.

author: blu
body: The marker is `Page` `N` [`of` `M`]. is-page-marker has already established the `Page` and the N, so the M is a lookahead past them: the token after N is the lowercase identifier `of`, and the one after that is the count. A page with no `of` reports M as 0, which is what the k > 1 rule rejects.

author: blu
body: On saturation an EMPTY document is returned, not the truncated one, and that is the LEX lesson rather than a second discovery of it: the is-done wind-down converts six linked lists with __linked-list-to-list and then anchors the prose blocks against the defs, all onto the deck that has just refused to grow, in proportion to everything collected so far. A late fire has far more to convert than any flat band covers. Nothing reads the document either way -- compile-parse raises CDX9002 for the phase and the compile halts on it.

author: blu
body: Runs once, when the Document is assembled. A template that carries a name is the author's explicit claim about which definition the block describes, therefore the claimed name wins. Every other block anchors to the definition that follows it in the source: the nearest def or type-def whose name token sits past the block's line. Blocks, defs, and type-defs each arrive in source order, therefore one merge walk anchors every block in a single pass.

author: blu
body: Named for this chapter because `Types--Type Checker` defines its own `find-def-index` over `List ADef`, reading `.name.value` off a desugared definition where this one reads `token-text` off a parsed one. They are two functions that answer the same question about different trees, not a duplicate to merge -- so the prefix is the fix and sharing the name would be the defect. Both callers happen to sit in the chapter that defines the version they want, which is the only reason the collision was latent rather than a miscompile.

author: blu
body: The check reads the block's anchor, not the template's name. For a named template the anchoring pass has already copied the claimed name into the anchor, therefore the two agree by construction; reading the anchor is what makes the anchor the association of record rather than a parallel bookkeeping the emitter carries and nothing consults.

author: blu
body: A chapter that declares no definitions still counts as present in the compilation unit. ChapterAssignment is built per DEFINITION, so a chapter carrying only an effect or a type declaration produced no assignment and check-cites-resolve reported it missing while it sat in the unit -- CDX3007 fired on every cite of Foreword chapter Console, which declares two effect operations and nothing else. The scan therefore accumulates every chapter header it passes, the way it already accumulates section titles.
